Face ID engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Face ID workflow covers storefront language. Xcode, entitlements, and Connect actually separate device unlock behavior from product-page copy:

  • Face ID capability — toggled in Xcode for apps that authenticate with biometrics. Controls whether the app can call LocalAuthentication. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • LocalAuthentication / LAContext — Swift APIs that present the system unlock sheet. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains instant unlock to buyers.
  • canEvaluatePolicy & biometryType — runtime checks for Face ID vs Touch ID availability. Your listing may mention both; detecting device class is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Secure Enclave & Keychain — where credentials are stored after a successful scan. Configuring storage is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • Privacy nutrition labels — App Store Connect privacy questionnaire when biometrics touch user data. Filing accurate answers is compliance work — AppLocale does not complete it for you.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Face ID flags in the binary.

A working Face ID integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Face ID–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Biometric-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Face ID feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Face ID phrasing

US pages use "Face ID", "Unlock with Face ID", "Sign in with Face ID", or "Face ID login." Apple's official Simplified Chinese storefront vocabulary uses 面容 ID for the feature name and 用面容 ID 解锁 for unlock flows. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing biometric capabilities your app does not support.

Unlock vs login vs confirm

Screenshot overlays differ by use case — app launch unlock, account login, payment confirmation, or vault access. Chinese buyers expect concise verbs: 解锁 for unlock, 登录 for login, 确认 for payment confirm. Mixing English "Sign in" with Chinese body copy on the same frame looks inconsistent.

Touch ID as a related search phrase

When your English listing mentions Touch ID fallback on older iPhones, AppLocale can weave 触控 ID into keywords or description where it matches your product — China buyers on legacy devices search both terms. The primary H1 angle and hero screenshot overlays stay Face ID and 面容 ID unless you scope otherwise.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need biometric-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 面容解锁, 刷脸登录, and 生物识别解锁 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Common mistakes on Face ID zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Face ID integration localizes automatically — capability enabled; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US Face ID badges verbatim — Latin "Unlock with Face ID" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with setup instructions — description explains how to enroll Face ID in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Translating the in-app permission string only — system unlock sheet may show Chinese from iOS while the App Store product page stays English
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement LocalAuthentication — LAContext, canEvaluatePolicy, biometryType checks, and Secure Enclave flows are outside listing rewrite
  • Cloning passkey or Sign in with Apple copy — Face ID unlock marketing is a different buyer story; see related guides above instead of reusing login-badge paragraphs
